 I really love Deep, and honestly all four hosts bring their own energy to the show, which is exactly why it works.

But sometimes I feel we, as an internet generation, have started typing the first harsh thought that comes to mind without pausing to feel the moment. That’s what this comment section reminded me of .. a lot of noise, a lot of quick judgments, and very little empathy. It actually reminded me of Good Luck, Have Fun, Don’t Die movie - the way technology and constant online energy can distort our reactions and make us less human in the way we respond. That’s why I’m saying, maybe let’s not turn every awkward moment into hate.

Lavari is meant to be fun.

Kevi Rite Jaish and Bey Yaar is when Gujarati movie industry took a turn to make meaningful and truly entertaining cinema and I always felt Abhishek Jain to be the saviour of Gujarati cinema. But I had never heard him speak. This is the first time I heard him speak. And I felt so embarrassed to have so much respect for him. They say never meet your idols - and Abhishek Jain proved it. He kept on showing arrogance and superiority complex in both parts. No matter how great work one does, there is no alternative to humility. Suddenly the great work you did starts to look very ordinary. Clearly Abhishek Jain needs to have a humble pie. He needs to learn to respect others. The Comedy Factory has grown so much in last two years - all four have been doing fantastic work. Keep up the great work.

This was such an amazing Gujarati web series! I’ve watched many Gujarati films and web series, and I’m mostly a romance person, so I absolutely love romantic stories with a little drama. ❤️ I’m also a huge K-drama lover, and honestly, while watching this series, I got such a K-drama vibe! The innocent and beautiful gestures by the boy, his sweet nature—totally a green flag! 💚 And Jaini’s character was so good—career-oriented, independent, and thodi si jhalli type, which made her even more relatable and lovable. 😄❤️ There’s so much good work happening in the Gujarati industry, especially in the romance genre, and I can definitely add this web series to my list of favourites. ✨ The acting was fantastic, the plot was beautifully written, and most importantly, nothing felt overdramatic or forced. The characters felt real, and you could genuinely connect with them. Really appreciate the entire team for creating something this beautiful. 👏❤️ I hope we get to see many more Gujarati web series like this in the future!

In karnataka and also Tamil Nadu- we call it bagala Bhaath- we cook the rice a bit soft and well done- donuts soft and mushy hot and we sometimes even add a little milk hot first in hot rice to make it mashed well mushy n creamy soft so it tastes extra creamy soft- then we add thick sour curds to the mashed soft rice add salt and mix well then add grated thin carrots , some fine chopped or grated skinned and seeded cucumbers too if we have fresh ones at home- yes and you can add pomegranate seeds for a seeet tangy taste some people add green grapes too for sweet sour taste - then put tadka of mustard seeds chana dal urad dal curry leaves , dhania leaves , 1/4 th piece ginger , chopped or slit green chillies without seeds n directed chillies too if you like it spicy - add this tadka and mix well with curd rice n enjoy Bagala Bhaath! *"Recipe: Crispy Veg Cutlets"* *_Ingredients:-_* *For the Vegetable Mixture:* * Boiled Potatoes: 4 medium (peeled and mashed) * Paneer: ½ cup (grated) * Carrots: ½ cup (grated) * Capsicum: ¼ cup (finely chopped) * Onion: ¼ cup (finely chopped) * Green Chilies: 1 tbsp (finely chopped) * Coriander Leaves: ¼ cup (finely chopped) * Chili Flakes: 1 tsp * Mixed Herbs / Oregano: 1 tsp * Black Pepper Powder: 1/3 tsp * Lemon Juice: 1 tbsp (can substitute with Amchur or Chaat Masala) * Salt: To taste * (Optional: You can also add finely chopped cabbage, beans, or spinach) *For the Slurry (Coating):* * Corn Flour: 4 tbsp * All-Purpose Flour (Maida): 4 tbsp * Black Pepper Powder: A pinch * Salt: A pinch * Water: As needed to make a thick batter *For the Outer Layer:* * Bread Crumbs: As required * Oil: For deep frying *_Instructions:-_* *1. Prepare the Vegetable Base* In a large mixing bowl, combine the mashed potatoes, grated paneer, carrots, capsicum, onions, green chilies, and coriander leaves. Add the chili flakes, mixed herbs, black pepper powder, salt, and lemon juice. Mix everything thoroughly by hand, ensuring the potatoes are well mashed and the spices are evenly distributed. *2. Shape the Cutlets* Clean your hands and take a small portion of the mixture. Roll it between your palms and shape it as desired. You can make them oval, egg-shaped, or the traditional round flat shape. Repeat until all the mixture is used. *3. Prepare the Coating Slurry* In a separate bowl, mix equal parts corn flour and maida (4 tbsp each). Add a pinch of salt and pepper. Gradually add water and whisk until you achieve a smooth, thick batter. Ensure it is not too thin. *4. Coat the Cutlets* Place the bread crumbs in a plate. Take a shaped cutlet and dip it into the flour slurry using a fork (this helps drain the excess batter). Immediately place it onto the bread crumbs and coat it evenly on all sides, tapping gently to ensure the crumbs stick. * Pro Tip: For extra crispiness and to prevent the cutlet from breaking in oil, you can do a "Double Coating" by dipping the bread-crumbed cutlet back into the slurry and then into the bread crumbs a second time. *5. Fry the Cutlets* Heat oil in a pan on medium to medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot, carefully place the cutlets in the pan. Avoid low heat as it will make the cutlets soggy; high heat ensures they turn crispy. Fry until they reach a dark golden brown color, flipping them occasionally to ensure even cooking. *6. Serving* Remove the cutlets and place them on a kitchen paper towel to drain any excess oil. Serve these hot and crispy veg cutlets with tomato ketchup or green chutney. Note: You can store these prepared, uncooked cutlets in an airtight container in the freezer. When ready to eat, take them out an hour before and deep fry or air fry them directly.
